Bootstrap uncertainty for the fast AME estimator

Source: R/ame_als_bootstrap.R
ame_als_bootstrap.Rd

Computes bootstrap standard errors and percentile confidence intervals for a fast AME fit produced by ame_als or lame_als. Two strategies are available:

parametric

(default) Simulates fresh outcomes from the fitted model on the response scale and refits. Available for both cross-sectional and longitudinal fits.

block

Resamples time slices with replacement. With block_length = 1 slices are resampled independently; block_length > 1 draws contiguous blocks (a moving-block bootstrap), which preserves short-run temporal dependence. Longitudinal fits only, and only when the panel supplies at least ceiling(T / block_length) >= 10 resampling blocks: below that the ends of the interval are the extreme replicates (a plain percentile interval covered the dyadic coefficient in 0.83 of the panels at five blocks), so the call says so and uses parametric instead. The returned object records the scheme actually used in type and the one asked for in requested_type. The interval end points are read at expanded percentile levels, and the parameters that vary over actors and not over time keep the analytic standard errors of the fit; see Block bootstrap below.

Every replicate is refit by ame_als_refit, warm-started from the original point estimate so that replicates do not drift to different local optima. Every replicate is refit with the empirical-Bayes estimator of the fit (see ame_als), re-estimating the covariance of the actor effects from the fitted one; the replicate effects are drawn in the fitted coordinates (uncentred for ame_als(), centred for lame_als()) and every refit is summarised as the fit reports it. The intervals then describe the empirical-Bayes estimator, and agree with the Laplace standard errors of vcov.ame_als where those are calibrated. A dynamic fit (lame(..., method = "als") with dynamic_ab, dynamic_beta or dynamic_uv) carries its own standard errors in vcov(), confint() and summary() (Laplace ones for a binary or Poisson fit, the exact Gaussian marginal ones for a normal fit) and has no bootstrap: bootstrap = N on such a fit leaves it with them and a message, and ame_als_bootstrap() refuses it with an error of class "lame_dynamic_eb_unsupported" before the replicate count is checked. A fit saved by an earlier release with a fast-route estimator setting that this release no longer has stops with an error of class "lame_als_removed_setting"; refit the model first. Standard errors are replicate column standard deviations; confidence intervals use the percentile method.

Replicates. At least 10 valid replicates are needed (R below 10 is an error of class "lame_als_bootstrap_replicates"; bootstrap = N in ame_als and lame_als needs 30, and a 95 percent percentile interval is best read from 200 or more). A replicate whose refit has not converged is retried on the same data with four times the budget and, failing that, dropped: it never enters an interval. A replicate that errors or returns non-finite values is dropped too, and every dropped replicate is counted (n_failed, with the reason in fail_reason). A dropped replicate is usually an extreme one, so the nominal level of a percentile interval can move by at most the share dropped; more than 5 percent of the R replicates dropped is an error of class "lame_als_bootstrap_convergence", raised at the replicate that crosses the cap, with no interval from the rest. Through bootstrap = N in ame_als, lame_als, ame and lame a bootstrap that stops with an error leaves the fit with its analytic standard errors and a message of class "lame_als_bootstrap_not_run".

One optimum per replicate. Every replicate is refit from the variational state of the fit. A normal-family replicate whose warm refit does not converge is also refit from a cold spectral start and, with a multiplicative term, from seven random starts, and the converged refit with the lowest objective is kept. The start each replicate kept is in boot_refit_start, and optimum_check says what was compared. The point estimate of every coefficient should lie inside the central 95 percent of its own replicates: if it does not, the replicates are distributed around another optimum, or the estimator is biased by more than two standard errors, and the coefficient takes the analytic standard error and Wald interval of the fit instead, named in coef_uncentred with the estimate and the replicate range. A variance component whose estimate lies outside its replicate interval is the bias of its estimator in a regime a percentile interval cannot describe (the variance of the lognormal layer of a count network without extra-Poisson noise is the usual case): it takes the analytic standard error and interval of the fit, it is named in vc_uncentred, and the rest of the bootstrap stands.

Block bootstrap. A statistic that varies over \(B\) resampling blocks has a percentile interval that falls short of its level. The end points of a block interval are therefore read at the expanded percentile levels \(\Phi(\sqrt{B / (B - 1)}\, t_{B - 1, \alpha / 2})\) (Hesterberg, 2015): 0.9 and 99.1 percent for a 95 percent interval at ten blocks, 1.6 and 98.4 percent at twenty. n_blocks records \(B\), and confint(), tidy() and the interval columns of print() and summary() use these levels. The number of replicates matters more here than for a parametric bootstrap, since the end points sit in the tails of the replicates: use 200 or more.

A block resample redraws the time slices and holds the actors fixed, so it carries the variability of the data over time and none of the variability over actors. The parameters whose sampling variability is that over actors have no replicate standard error under type = "block": they take the analytic standard errors and intervals of the fit, are named in withheld and se_source with the reason, and print() and summary() say so. type = "parametric" gives replicate ones. They are the node-covariate coefficients, va, vb and cab, the intercept when the model has node covariates (it refers to the uncentred covariates, so it carries their coefficients) and the additive effects and factors, which are shrunk toward their prior mean: the replicates vary around the shrunk estimates, not around the effects. The residual variance ve has none either: a refit to a resample, which repeats some slices and omits others, absorbs more of the noise than the original fit, so its replicates sit below the estimate. The intercept is the mean of the linear predictor over the observed actors (the additive effects sum to zero), and its interval is for that quantity and not for a population intercept.

On simulated directed normal panels (20 actors, 12 to 20 periods, 160 panels, 200 replicates; a time-varying dyadic covariate, static node covariates, random actor effects and reciprocal errors) the block intervals covered the dyadic coefficient in 0.96 to 1.00 of the panels and rho in 0.93 to 0.98, and the intercept in 0.03 to 0.13, the node-covariate coefficients in 0.05 to 0.10, va, vb and cab in 0.02 to 0.18 and the additive effects in 0.27 to 0.39, which is why those take the analytic errors of the fit; ve covered 0.91 to 0.95 and has no interval. The variances va and vb are biased upward by an amount that does not scale with them, and their replicates reproduce the bias (a percentile interval covered 0.65 to 0.75 of the panels), so their parametric intervals are the basic (bias-corrected) interval (0.91 to 0.97 at 20 and 30 actors).

Usage

ame_als_bootstrap(
  object,
  R = 200,
  type = c("parametric", "block"),
  block_length = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  max_iter = 200L,
  tol = 1e-06
)

Arguments

object

an ame_als object from ame_als or lame_als.

R

integer number of bootstrap replicates (default 200); at least 10. A block bootstrap reads the ends of its interval from the tails of the replicates, so use 200 or more.

type

"parametric" (default) or "block"; see Description.

block_length

block length for the block bootstrap: 1 (default) resamples time slices independently; an integer > 1 draws contiguous blocks of that many slices (a moving-block bootstrap), appropriate when the series has short-run temporal dependence. Capped at T; ignored for the parametric bootstrap.

seed

optional integer random seed.

verbose

logical; print progress (default TRUE).

max_iter

positive integer iteration budget for each refit (default 200). A replicate that does not converge is retried on the same data with four times this budget. A normal-family refit that still fails also tries a fresh spectral start and, with a multiplicative term, seven starts from the fixed internal seed 6886, keeping the converged refit with the lowest objective. A replicate that still has not converged is dropped, and more than 5 percent dropped is an error.

tol

positive convergence tolerance for each refit (default 1e-6).

Value

An object of class "boot_ame" with components including coefs (replicate intercept + regression coefficients), se, ci_lo, ci_hi, point_est, param_names; vc_* for the variance components; a_coefs, b_coefs, se_a, se_b; U_aligned, V_aligned, U_raw, V_raw, se_U, se_V (when R > 0 and the factors are static; the analytic ones of the fit for the columns whose singular values are not separated), sv_separation (the singular values of the point estimate, the gaps and their z-scores in bootstrap standard deviations, the threshold, and which columns are resolved) and subspace (the principal angles, in degrees, of the replicate factor spaces to the point estimate's, and their largest angle by side); n_valid, n_total, n_failed, fail_reason (per replicate: "", "nonconverged", "error" or "nonfinite"), max_fail_share, boot_refit_start (the start each replicate kept), optimum_check, n_other_start (replicates that kept a start other than the warm one), coef_uncentred and vc_uncentred (the coefficients and variance components whose replicates are not centred on the estimate, when there are any), withheld (a data frame of the parameters the scheme gives no replicate standard error, their kind — "coefficient" or "vc" or "effects" — and the reason; NULL when the replicates cover every parameter), se_source (the parameters whose standard error and interval are the analytic ones of the fit, with the reason; NULL when there are none), analytic (those analytic errors), n_blocks (the number of resampling blocks of a block bootstrap, NA otherwise), type, family.

Details

Choice of inference. Every fit already carries Laplace standard errors (vcov.ame_als). The bootstrap, which mirrors sir::boot_sir(), gives the replicate distribution of the estimator instead; its intervals agree with the Laplace ones where those are calibrated.

Alignment-sensitive quantities. The regression coefficients beta, the additive effects a, b and the variance components are rotation-invariant and are aggregated directly. The multiplicative factors U, V are not: each replicate is Procrustes-aligned to the original fit before its standard errors are computed. The object stores both the raw and aligned replicate factors so the effect of alignment can be inspected. The alignment identifies a column only when its singular value is separated from its neighbours': two adjacent singular values (eigenvalues, for a symmetric model) count as separated when their gap in the point estimate is at least 5 bootstrap standard deviations of that gap (sv_separation$threshold; the rotation the alignment applies to the pair is then under 4 degrees at the median and under 10 at the 90th percentile, against 9 and 25 when the two are equal). The U and V columns that are not separated from a neighbour take the analytic posterior standard deviations of the fit (fit$U_sd, fit$V_sd) for the column-wise standard errors (se_U, se_V, and their unaligned _raw versions) and Wald intervals in confint(). What is reported for every fit with a multiplicative term, separated or not, is the uncertainty of the subspaces the factors span, which a rotation of the columns does not change: the principal angles, in degrees, between each replicate's row-factor (and column-factor) space and the point estimate's (subspace). For a symmetric model the eigenvalues L of the multiplicative term are aggregated and reported as well.

The parametric bootstrap is a full parametric bootstrap of the AME model: each replicate draws fresh additive random effects a, b from their fitted dispersion (va, vb, cab) and fresh residuals, holding mu, beta and the multiplicative term fixed. Regenerating the additive effects (rather than holding the fitted a, b fixed) is what gives the intercept and node-covariate standard errors their actor-level sampling-variability component.

Assumptions. The block bootstrap treats the time slices as exchangeable replicates of the static-effects model — appropriate for that model, but not for strongly trended or serially dependent series (use the dynamic lame there). The block bootstrap needs at least ten resampling blocks, so parametric (the default) is substituted, with a warning, on a panel that supplies fewer than ten blocks. The MCMC ame / lame path gives posterior summaries when that is the target.

References

Minhas, S. and Hoff, P. D. (2025). Decomposing Network Dynamics: Social Influence Regression. Political Analysis. The block and parametric bootstrap follow the inference scheme of sir::boot_sir() developed for the SIR estimator.

Hesterberg, T. C. (2015). What teachers should know about the bootstrap: resampling in the undergraduate statistics curriculum. The American Statistician 69(4), 371–386.

See also

ame_als and lame_als, both of which accept bootstrap = N, bootstrap_type, bootstrap_block_length, bootstrap_seed to do this work in a single call when you are about to fit the model anyway. ame_als_bootstrap() is the post-hoc path (bootstrap an already-fit object without refitting from scratch). ame_als_refit for warm-start refits; confint.boot_ame for the bootstrap CI extractor.

Author

Cassy Dorff, Shahryar Minhas, Tosin Salau

Examples

# \donttest{
# twelve periods supply the ten resampling blocks the block scheme needs
Y <- replicate(12, { m <- matrix(rnorm(225), 15, 15); diag(m) <- NA; m },
               simplify = FALSE)
fit <- lame_als(Y, R = 1, family = "normal", verbose = FALSE)
# post-hoc bootstrap of an existing fit:
bt <- ame_als_bootstrap(fit, R = 50, type = "block",
                            seed = 1, verbose = FALSE)
# equivalent one-shot call:
# fit_b <- lame_als(Y, R = 1, family = "normal", verbose = FALSE,
#                   bootstrap = 50, bootstrap_type = "block",
#                   bootstrap_seed = 1)
print(bt)
#> 
#> Bootstrap results: fast AME estimator
#> Type: block | Family: normal | Replicates: 50/50 valid
#> 
#>           Estimate Boot SE    2.5%  97.5%
#> intercept  -0.0021  0.0216 -0.0425 0.0458
#> 
#> beta, a, b and variance components aggregate directly; U/V are
#> Procrustes-aligned.
#> Block resample of 12 blocks: the interval ends are the 1.1% and 98.9% quantiles
#> of the replicates.
#> Analytic standard errors and intervals for va, cab, vb, where the bootstrap
#> gives none: slice resampling holds the actors fixed, and the sampling
#> variability of the variances of the actor effects is that over actors.
#> Analytic standard errors and intervals for a, b, U, V, where the bootstrap
#> gives none: the effects of this estimator are shrunk toward their prior mean,
#> and the replicates of a resample vary around the shrunk estimates, not around
#> the effects.
#> Analytic standard errors and intervals for ve, where the bootstrap gives none:
#> the refit to resampled slices, which repeat some and omit others, absorbs more
#> of the noise than the original fit, so the replicate residual variances sit
#> below the estimate.
#> `type = "parametric"` gives intervals for them.
# }
